item.title: Kyle DeVan’s Intensity Drives Bears Offensive Line Success
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears offensive line found its voice not with a cheer, but with a scowl. After a win against the New England Patriots, assistant coach Kyle DeVan looked like someone had shot his dog, according to reports. This was not a moment of celebration for the 41-year-old coach, even though the team won from start to finish on a short week. DeVan explained his reaction with brutal honesty, stating, “I want to win every game and I want us to play the best we can, and when we don’t, I get a little not happy,” per the Chicago Tribune . That specific intensity is now the fuel the Bears are betting on to fix their line issues. Johnson’s Deliberate Plan Head coach Ben Johnson did not stumble into this pairing by accident. The Bears constructed Johnson’s first staff in February 2025 with a clear goal: find a younger assistant to work in tandem with veteran Dan Roushar. Johnson wants to develop young draft picks like Luke Newman into future starters once veterans move on. He openly admits that he drops DeVan’s name regularly on purpose to get him noticed by other teams. “I’m glad you caught that,” Johnson said of his references to DeVan, noting that the spotlight is by intent, per the Chicago Tribune. This strategy helps DeVan grow while keeping the Bears’ development pipeline strong. Strength in the Trenches The physical preparation for this line goes beyond just blocking schemes. Assistant strength and conditioning coach Mark Philippi brings a unique background that has the internet buzzing. A former world champion powerlifter, Philippi has qualified for the World’s Strongest Man competition seven times. Christian D’Andrea of For The Win joked that Philippi is the “final boss all other strength coaches must strive to defeat,” according to Sports Illustrated . Some fans even suggested the team should “suit up Mark Philippi” to solve their offensive line problems. Philippi’s presence ensures the players have the raw power to match DeVan’s technical demands. A Lesson in Celebration DeVan eventually learned that a win is hard to do and deserves a moment of joy. After being fined $100 by his linemen for his lack of celebration, he adjusted his approach. “I learned my lesson,” DeVan said. “I celebrate everything. I’ve been in this thing. A win is hard to do,” per the Chicago Tribune. This shift shows a coach who cares deeply about the process but respects the final result. The Bears face a tough test on Thursday, Nov. 26, at Ford Field against the Detroit Lions.

item.title: How Micah Ford flipped ignominious era for Stanford football into his personal legacy
item.description: Micah Ford #20 of the Stanford Cardinal looks on before a game against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets on Sept. 26, 2026 at Stanford Stadium in Palo Alto, Calif. (Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Micah Ford has witnessed the lows of this Stanford football era. In November 2024, as a freshman, he watched from the California Memorial Stadium sideline as quarterback Fernando Mendoza went "98 yards with my boys" to lead an epic Big Game comeback, handing Stanford its first four-game losing streak against Cal since 2005. He was in the building four months later, when recently hired general manager Andrew Luck fired Troy Taylor, the head coach who had recruited him, citing the need for a "reset" after an investigation concluded that Taylor had bullied and belittled female staffers. Ford saw all of it. The 3-9 season in 2024. The 4-8 campaign a year ago. The slow start this season. He played for one head coach as a freshman (Taylor), then another as a sophomore (interim Frank Reich), and now another as a junior playing for first-year head coach Tavita Pritchard. Chaos and turmoil were all he knew. Midway through October, the feeling couldn't have been much better. The Cardinal were 2-4, and each blowout loss looked worse than the last. His team lost those games by a combined 172 points. Ford, the engine of the offense at running back, wasn't producing. But after that 58-7 loss to then-No. 6 Notre Dame on Oct. 10, something changed. Stanford, led by Ford's sudden emergence, became an unrecognizable football team. The first six games of Ford's season: 95 carries, 350 yards (3.7 yards per carry) and four rushing touchdowns. The last five: 108 carries, 701 yards (6.5 YPC) and nine rushing touchdowns. His yardage totals, including receptions, in each of those games were 231, 208, 120, 150 and 156. He's been the most consistent presence for an offense that desperately needed it under fourth-year running backs coach Malcolm Agnew. Ford's success directly led to Stanford's (6-5, 4-4 ACC) success. The Cardinal have won four of their last five games. They destroyed Cal 44-28 in Saturday's Big Game and earned bowl-game eligibility for the first time since 2018. Looking back, Ford can easily say it was all worth it. "To be at a program where, obviously, I didn't have success early, and then to see it gel into the program that we knew it could be," Ford said Saturday, "it's kind of just, like, I'm at a loss of words for it. "Honestly, there was no way we were leaving without that axe today," he added, after rushing for 151 yards and two touchdowns. "I don't know how long (it's been since) Stanford kept it two years in a row. It's probably been a little while." Ford is correct. The last time Stanford won consecutive games against Cal was in 2018, the last of a dominant nine-year Big Game run. Following that season, the Bears won five of six matchups from 2019-2024. item.title: MLB Pitch-Rigging Case Turns to Shocking Personal Texts
item.description: Jul 26, 2025; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Cleveland Guardians relief pitcher Emmanuel Clase (48) delivers a pitch against the Kansas City Royals in the ninth inning at Kauffman Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images The federal trial of former Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz continues this week in Brooklyn, with testimony focusing on the two June 2025 pitches prosecutors say Ortiz deliberately threw outside the strike zone in exchange for payments. Jurors have heard from a FanDuel executive that six wagers on Ortiz’s first pitch of the third inning on June 27 against the Cardinals generated more than $19,000 in winnings and led the sportsbook to suspend four accounts the next day. Those same accounts had also placed bets on an Ortiz pitch from June 15. Prosecutors argue those flagged bets helped launch the broader investigation. A cooperating witness, Enthony Diaz, has testified that he netted more than $31,000 on wagers tied to the two pitches Ortiz is accused of rigging. On the same June 27 date, prosecutors introduced WhatsApp messages between Ortiz and his wife that included the lines “Delete the evidence,” “What if he’s undercover?” and “Luis, it’s your future.” Ortiz has pleaded not guilty. His defense maintains he never communicated with the bettors and that the government’s case against him is thin. Clase, the former All-Star closer, is accused of providing information on roughly 18 pitches across three seasons (beginning in 2023) and recruiting Ortiz into the scheme in 2025. Both players face charges of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, honest-services wire fraud, sports bribery, and money laundering. They remain on unpaid leave from the Guardians and are considered highly unlikely to pitch in the majors again regardless of the trial outcome. Prosecutors have indicated they expect to rest their case around Thanksgiving, with closing arguments and a possible verdict in early December. MLB continues its own investigation parallel to the criminal proceedings.

item.title: Yaya on Brazil's mood and why friendlies matter for the World Cup
item.description: Yaya on Brazil's mood and why friendlies matter for the World Cup The second player to arrive in Hiroshima, Japan, midfielder Vitória Yaya spoke about her expectations for Brazil’s final fixtures of 2026. Called up for the two friendlies against Japan, the Paris Saint-Germain player discussed what it feels like to reunite with her Brazil teammates and how the atmosphere differs from everyday life at her club. “Getting together with the girls on the national team is incredible; it’s a completely different atmosphere. We know each other and share that Brazilian spirit, which is something I miss a little over there (at the club). It’s always great to be around people from Brazil, and it does me good,” she said. Looking ahead to the matches against Japan, the midfielder emphasized how challenging the games would be and the opportunity to face a team with unique qualities. Yaya also highlighted the importance of playing against national teams with different styles during this World Cup preparation cycle, as Brazil do not yet know who their opponents will be in the tournament. “I believe these two matches will teach us a lot and be very difficult. Brazil’s main challenge will be man-to-man marking because Japan are a team that moves around a lot, but we’ll be ready for that.” “It’s always good to prepare by playing strong teams, and considering we still don’t know our World Cup opponents, having faced a variety of opponents will be very good for us,” she concluded. Brazil’s women’s national team will face Japan twice. The first friendly will take place on Sunday (29) at 1:55 a.m. (Brasília time) at Edion Peace Wing Stadium in Hiroshima. The second match is scheduled for December 5 at 3 a.m. (Brasília time) at JFE Harenokuni Stadium in Okayama. item.description: Kansas City quarterback Patrick Mahomes, left, and Buffalo quarterback Josh Allen, right, will lead their clubs into an NFL Thanksgiving holiday showdown with the best record in the NFL's American Conference up for grabs (David Eulitt) Kansas City quarterback Patrick Mahomes and Buffalo superstar Josh Allen face a Thursday showdown on the US Thanksgiving holiday that will have a major impact on the NFL playoff picture. The Bills own the AFC's best record at 9-1 and beating the Chiefs (8-2) would help ensure a home-field edge in the post-season. "We know what type of team they are," Allen said. "They've been one of the best teams in the league the last 10 years. So, you've got to play your best." Mahomes, whose club shares the AFC West division lead with Denver, hopes to snap Buffalo's six-game win streak. "It will be a great challenge for us. We're excited for it," Mahomes said. "You know it's going to take your best football. "Every time we play each other, it always comes down to the end of the game. It's about who makes the big plays in the big moments. It's always exciting. It's always fun." The Bills have averaged 31 points in their win streak while the Chiefs have won three in a row with 34 or more points each game. Allen's Bills and Mahomes's Chiefs are 5-5 in all-time meetings, but it's not so even when it comes to realizing and crushing title hopes. Allen and the Bills are 5-1 in regular-season matchups against Kansas City but Mahomes and the Chiefs are 4-0 in playoff games against Buffalo. The Chiefs have won three Super Bowls and lost two others in the past seven seasons while the Bills have not reached the Super Bowl since losing four in a row from 1991-1994 and were eliminated from the playoffs by Kansas City in four of the past six seasons. "It's the most important one because it's the next one," Allen said of the game. "All the seeding implications, that is what it is. We're just trying to find a way to go 1-0 each week." item.title: Sidney Crosby wants to be a ‘Penguin forever’, agent claims
item.description: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Sidney Crosby wants to be a ‘Penguin forever’, agent claims appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Penguins are mired in a disappointing season so far in the NHL. Pittsburgh has reportedly been considering moving Sidney Crosby , ahead of the league’s trade deadline. Crosby’s agent is now throwing cold water on that idea. “His goal is to be a Penguin forever,” Crosby’s agent Pat Brisson said, per Sportsnet. Crosby has played his entire NHL career in Pittsburgh. He is a fan-favorite in that city, and has helped lead the Penguins to three Stanley Cup championships. item.title: Paul Pierce Admits 2013 Trade Built Current Celtics Core
item.description: Neville E. Guard-Imagn Images The Boston Celtics won the 2024 NBA title, but the foundation was laid when the franchise traded away its biggest star. Paul Pierce, the man who led the team to victory in 2008, says he has zero regrets about leaving in 2013. He knows the picks Boston received from that deal turned into the two players who finally brought the trophy back. The Trade That Changed Everything Back in 2013, the Brooklyn Nets were desperate and desperate teams make mistakes. They traded for Pierce and Kevin Garnett, giving up three unprotected first-round picks and a pick swap. The Nets project failed hard, and the assets Boston got in return became the keys to the kingdom. According to HITC , Pierce told the Amongst Legends podcast that the trade was handled with total transparency. He respected the process even though it meant leaving Boston. When the Nets finished with a 21-61 record in 2016, Boston used the number three overall pick to draft Jaylen Brown. The next year, the Celtics exercised their pick swap after Brooklyn had the worst record in the league. In the 2017 Draft, Danny Ainge traded down to let the Sixers select Markelle Fultz while the Lakers chose Lonzo Ball. Boston then swooped in to select Jayson Tatum with the third pick. Those two young stars led the team to a championship in 2024, defeating the Mavericks in the Finals. Pierce Owns The Legacy Many fans might think trading Pierce was a mistake, but he sees it differently now. He says the current success of the franchise rests on the foundation his departure created. A Look Back at California Roots Conner Henry, a native of Claremont, California, is part of that long history. He was selected by the Houston Rockets in the 1988 NBA Draft, but he had signed with Boston in 1987. His time with the team was short, lasting only until he was cut that fall. item.description: Nick Wosika-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The Minnesota Wild have never had more points through 26 games than they do right now. That win was also Filip Gustavsson’s first regular-season start since April 13 and his first appearance of 2026-27. Last year’s starter stopped 22 of 24 shots in his return from long-term injured reserve . When the Wild activated him Monday, they placed Quinn Hughes on injured reserve. Putting Hughes on IR let Calvin Pickard stay on the roster for now, giving Minnesota three goalies on the active roster. Last night in San Jose, Pickard backed up Gustavsson while starter Jesper Wallstedt got the night off. Minnesota Wild place Calvin Pickard on waivers On Tuesday afternoon, however, the Minnesota Wild announced that Pickard has been placed on waivers, an inevitable move after Gus Bus came back. If Pickard clears, he will go to Iowa, which would open up $1 million in cap space for Minnesota. Given the desperation around the league for competent goaltender depth, it’s very plausible he doesn’t make it that far. The result should come Wednesday. Until then, he technically remains on Minnesota’s NHL roster. item.title: Scottie Scheffler, Wyndham Clark headline PGA Tour Player of the Year finalists
item.description: Scottie Scheffler has another shot at PGA Tour Player of the Year, but he’ll have plenty of competition. Scheffler, Wyndham Clark, Matt Fitzpatrick, Chris Gotterup and Cameron Young were named Tuesday as the five finalists for the Jack Nicklaus Award, given annually to the PGA Tour Player of the Year. The Tour also announced five finalists for the Arnold Palmer Award as Rookie of the Year: Alex Fitzpatrick, Ben James, Jackson Koivun, Marco Penge and Kristoffer Reitan. Scheffler’s case starts with another huge season. The world No. 1 won three times, including the season-ending Tour Championship, claimed the FedEx Cup and led the Tour with 13 top-10 finishes in 20 starts. He also won the Byron Nelson Award with a 68.619 scoring average and missed just one cut. Clark also won three times in 25 starts, highlighted by the U.S. Open , along with victories at the CJ Cup Byron Nelson and BMW Championship. He finished the season with six top-10s. Matt Fitzpatrick matched that three-win total, taking the Valspar Championship, RBC Heritage and Zurich Classic of New Orleans. He posted eight top-10s in 21 starts and missed just one cut. Gotterup also made it a three-win season, capturing the Sony Open in Hawaii, WM Phoenix Open and John Deere Classic. He finished No. 4 in the FedEx Cup and recorded seven top-10s in 23 starts. Young is the only Player of the Year finalist with just two victories, but one of them was a big one. He won the Players Championship and later added the Cadillac Championship, finished with eight top-10s and didn’t miss a cut in 20 starts. The Rookie of the Year race features a mix of winners and some of the game’s most recognizable young players. Alex Fitzpatrick won the Zurich Classic alongside his brother, Matt, to secure his Tour card. He then went on to record six top-10 finishes and was one of only two rookies to reach the Tour Championship, finishing No. 4 in the FedEx Cup. Koivun, one of the biggest names to arrive from the college game, won the 3M Open and added three more top-10 finishes. He qualified for the FedEx Cup Playoffs despite having just five regular-season starts and earned a captain's pick for the 2026 U.S. Presidents Cup team. Penge capped his rookie season with a victory at the RSM Classic this past weekend , while Reitan won the Truist Championship and joined Fitzpatrick as the only other rookie to qualify for the Tour Championship. James didn’t notch a win but came close several times. He had runner-up finishes at the Biltmore Championship Asheville and World Wide Technology Championship, along with three other top-five finishes. He made 12 cuts in 14 starts after earning his card as the No. 1 player in the 2026 PGA Tour University ranking. The winners will be determined by a vote of PGA Tour members who competed in at least 15 official events during the 2026 season. item.description: Oct 12, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Kris Bubic (40) throws a pitch against the Milwaukee Brewers during the fifth inning in game two of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images The Cleveland Guardians made their first significant free-agent addition of the winter on Tuesday, agreeing to terms with left-hander Kris Bubic on a one-year, $17.5 million contract, according to multiple reports. The deal, which is pending a physical, is the largest one-year guarantee in franchise history and gives Cleveland a familiar AL Central arm to bolster a rotation that already features Parker Messick and Gavin Williams. Bubic, 29, was a 2025 American League All-Star with the Royals, posting a career-best 2.55 ERA over 116⅓ innings that season. His 2026 campaign was far more limited. Elbow and shoulder issues sidelined him for much of the year; he finished with a 3.76 ERA across 55 innings split between Kansas City and the Dodgers after a deadline trade. When healthy, he has shown a five-pitch mix built around a rising four-seam fastball, a firm changeup, and a pair of breaking balls, along with a delivery that has historically generated soft contact and ground balls. For Cleveland, the signing fits a clear priority. The Guardians entered the offseason looking to add starting pitching depth after a season in which they were the only team in baseball to have four pitchers make at least 30 starts. Bubic is expected to slot into the middle of a group that also includes Messick (2026 AL Rookie of the Year and Cy Young finalist), Williams (AL strikeout leader), Tanner Bibee, and several depth options. Outside the Bubic agreement, Cleveland’s offseason activity has been quiet and roster-focused. At the non-tender deadline, they non-tendered utility man David Fry, agreed to deals with relievers Matt Festa and Colin Holderman plus outfielder Blake Perkins to avoid arbitration, and have signed minor-league free agents (including right-hander Jairo Iriarte and left-hander Antoine Kelly). They also added several players to the 40-man roster and claimed José Tena off waivers. With the collective bargaining agreement set to expire December 1, the remaining window for additional moves is short . Bubic gives the Guardians an upside left-handed starter on a prove-it deal while they evaluate further pitching or lineup needs.

item.description: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images The National Football League has decided against suspending Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf after he was ejected during Sunday’s loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. This ruling comes despite Metcalf committing two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties that led to his removal from the game late in the third quarter. The league determined that a suspension was not warranted for the incident where Metcalf allegedly tried to poke Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean in the eye. While the suspension is off the table, the league will still review the conduct to see if a fine is necessary. Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy addressed the situation during his Monday media availability, noting that he and Metcalf had spoken about the event. McCarthy described the conversations between the two as “productive” and stated that any further discipline from the team would be kept internal. “Life’s about learning situations,” McCarthy said. He also expressed his belief in second chances, noting that he would judge Metcalf based on their personal interactions rather than just the penalty flags. A History of Discipline This ejection marks the third time in his eight-season career that Metcalf has been thrown out of a game. The final two games of the 2025 regular season carry a suspension for the player due to behavior stemming from a physical altercation with a Lions fan in Detroit. The financial toll on the player has been significant, with his fines totaling a whopping $245,647 according to reports. This total excludes an extra $555,555 fine associated with the two-game suspension resulting from the Lions fan altercation. After Sunday’s game, Metcalf exited the locker room without talking to reporters, though he came back to speak with the media on Monday. ProFootballTalk states that he rejected claims he intended to poke Cooper DeJean in the eye. With just one catch on four targets for two yards before ejection, the 28-year-old receiver struggled to find his rhythm this season. In 10 games, the two-time Pro Bowler has secured 36 of his 74 targets, accumulating 434 yards and only two touchdowns. Looking Ahead to Denver Metcalf remains on the Steelers’ active roster as they prepare for their next matchup. The team has a short week to recover before hosting the Denver Broncos at Acrisure Stadium. The game is scheduled for Friday, Nov. 27, with kickoff set for 3 p.m. ET. RotoBaller indicates that Metcalf currently sits as the WR40 in half-PPR scoring.

item.title: Dyson Daniels Proves The League Wrong On Value
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Dyson Daniels is the Atlanta Hawks’ most valuable player, not Jalen Johnson, because he drives wins without shooting. Soaring Down South reported that Daniels holds a staggering +18.0 on/off net rating to start the year. This number is the best on the team. The league thinks a shooter is needed to win. Daniels is changing that view with his defense and speed. He impacts winning in every way except shooting, which is a rare skill set. The Thompson twins are the only other players who succeed this way, but both are struggling this season. Amen Thompson has a -9.7 on/off rating with the Rockets, while Ausar sits at +2.2 with the Pistons. Daniels has surpassed both of them. A Deal That Saves The Hawks Money Daniels remains on a team-friendly deal of $25 million per year through the 2029-2030 season. He will have the 35th-highest salary in the league that year, making it the 23rd-lowest contract. Other players in his $20-30 million range include Damian Lillard, Herb Jones, and PJ Washington. Daniels is only 23 years old, one year younger than Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg. By the time his contract ends after the 2030 season, he will be 27 and entering his prime. The contract gives the Hawks an advantage over other teams.

item.title: Mahomes And Reid Show Chiefs Pride Supports Kansas City Current
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs did not wait for a press release to show support for their city. Patrick Mahomes and Andy Reid made their stance clear on Sunday at Arrowhead Stadium. While the team prepared for a matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, the focus shifted to a family moment that celebrated a local soccer title. Mahomes, dressed in his full uniform, stopped to greet his wife and children. This act of love happened right before kickoff on a cold November afternoon. A Family Moment on the Sideline The video of the reunion spread fast across social media after the league shared it. Mahomes was already in his red No. 15 jersey when he walked over to the sideline. His children were bundled up in warm coats against the chill. One daughter wore a pale pink puffer coat while the other stood close. The quarterback bent down to wrap his arms around both kids for hugs and kisses. He then turned his attention to Brittany Mahomes, who wore a long black coat. She reached up to touch his face before they shared a kiss. The NFL posted the clip on X with a simple note about the moment. They wrote, “@PatrickMahomes getting some pregame love from his favorite people,” according to Sports Illustrated . Fans React to the Tribute Local fans saw the connection between the NFL champion and the NWSL champions immediately. Brittany Mahomes had already shared photos of the Kansas City Current winning their title. Her husband and the head coach supported her, and the community took notice. People watching the feed reacted with warm words about the scene. One person commented, “Okay that hug actually got me,” per Sports Illustrated. Another viewer simply said, “They are adorable.” A third fan summed up the feeling of the day by writing, “pregame with the family hits different.” These comments show how much the city cares about all its teams, not just one. The Chiefs have built a culture that values family and local pride in equal measure. Mahomes and Reid proved that point without saying a word during the game. The team won their match against Arizona with a final score of 34 to 7 on Sunday. Now the squad looks ahead to their next challenge on the road. The Kansas City Chiefs will play the Buffalo Bills on Thursday, Nov. 26, at 8:20 p.m.

item.title: Sam Rinzel’s Historic Run Earns Third Star Honor
item.description: Sergei Belski-Imagn Images Sam Rinzel has finally gotten the recognition he deserves after a wild week of play. The NHL announced on Monday, Nov. 23, that the young defenseman earned the league’s Third Star of the Week. This marks a massive shift for a player many fans wanted benched just months ago. Rinzel recorded eight points in four games to secure the spot, joining Robert Thomas and Jake Oettinger on the weekly list. According to Blackhawk Up , this achievement makes him the first Blackhawks defenseman to grab this honor since Duncan Keith in December 2013. Rinzel posted 13 points in five games at the end of October, a run that included one goal and 12 assists. He also became only the fourth defenseman in NHL history to record multiple assists in five straight games. That list includes legends like Bobby Orr and Mark Howe. According to Blackhawk Up, his average ice time rose from 16 minutes in October to more than 21 minutes in November. The team trusts him now because he is delivering results on the ice. The first power-play unit he plays on has netted 10 goals across their last six games. The Confidence Shift Teammates and coaches point to one simple reason for this sudden change: confidence. Coach Jeff Blashill noted that the game has finally slowed down for the young defender. Frank Nazar told reporters that Rinzel has been playing with a lot of swagger. “He’s been really confident, playing with a lot of swagger. Him keeping pucks in the zone is a huge part of why he’s succeeding,” Nazar said. Alex Vlasic added that everything Rinzel touches seems to turn into a point lately. The player himself admits he is not overthinking things anymore. Rinzel said, “[I’m] not being afraid to just play — don’t think, just play.” He also noted that he still makes mistakes and has work to do, but the mindset is there. History in the Making Rinzel’s current mindset places him among the best offensive defenders in the league right now. As of Oct. 31, he sat third in the NHL in assists with 14, trailing only Connor McDavid and Kirill Kaprizov. The Blackhawks have gone 4-1-1 in their last six games, and Rinzel has been a huge part of that success. Although his five-game multi-point streak concluded on Sunday versus the Canucks, he performed well and almost recorded additional points. His ability to shoot and create chances has transformed the team’s offense. Regarding his historic run, Rinzel spoke after the game in Calgary, “It definitely wasn’t on my bucket list.” The Blackhawks have found a new leader on their blue line.

item.title: Lakers Target P.J. Washington To Strengthen Frontcourt
item.description: David Richard-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers are making moves to fix their frontcourt before the trade deadline arrives. General manager Rob Pelinka wants to shore up the team’s depth and add a reliable wing player. Reports indicate the club is targeting Dallas Mavericks forward P.J. Washington to fill a specific hole in their rotation. Heavy.com outlines a specific plan where Dallas sends Washington to Los Angeles in exchange for Jarred Vanderbilt, Jaden Hardy, and two future second-round picks. The Mavericks would receive the picks to add assets to their roster while clearing space for other players. This move would reunite Washington with Luka Doncic, his former teammate from Dallas. The Lakers see Washington as the missing piece to help their star trio dominate the playoffs. Why The Lakers Need Washington Los Angeles has struggled to find a consistent two-way player at the forward spot this season. The team needs someone who can guard top scorers and hit open shots without needing the ball. Heavy.com notes that Washington fits this exact profile. Washington is putting up solid numbers this year. While shooting 36.2% from three-point range, he averages 14.0 points, 6.7 rebounds, and 1.3 assists. Those stats show he can contribute immediately without disrupting the flow of the offense. The Lakers have been linked to him for a long time, but the salary cap makes it difficult. His $88 million contract is a big hurdle, yet the front office seems willing to take the risk. Backup Center Search Continues While chasing Washington, the Lakers are also looking for a backup center to play behind Walker Kessler. Marc Stein reported Sunday that the team is actively seeking help in the middle. “Lakers have been actively searching for another center to play behind Walker Kessler and general manager Rob Pelinka has all but promised that a move is forthcoming to address that need,” Stein wrote. The team has limited draft capital to use as leverage in these talks. One potential target is Mavericks center Moussa Cissé. Rookie guard Walter Clayton Jr. could be added to Dallas’s roster, which might require moving Cissé, and Stein noted that the Lakers have only three tradeable second‑round picks, highlighting their limited draft capital, though Los Angeles could trade Kevon Looney and a pick for Cissé despite the 24‑year‑old logging just 36 minutes this season. He is a gamble on upside rather than a sure thing. The Trade Deadline Approach Rob Pelinka has made it clear that the team plans to be active before the deadline. He spoke on Spectrum SportsNet about the need to fix issues the team has spotted. “We’ll be active at the trade deadline to shore up things that we see,” Pelinka said during a Spectrum SportsNet interview. The front office knows the roster has gaps that need filling if they want to challenge for a championship.

item.title: Guess Who Scored Another OT Goal for the Griffins?
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There’s not much more Grand Rapids Griffins forward John Leonard can do to show how his offensive touch might be able to help the Detroit Red Wings. Leonard scored an overtime goal for a Griffins-record third consecutive game to give the Griffins a 3-2 win against the Manitoba Moose in a Tuesday matinee game. It was his fifth consecutive game-winning goal for Leonard. The New Jersey native, brother of Washington Capitals player Ryan Leonard, showed two goals and an assist in the game. That gives him 13 goals in his past seven games and a league-leading 18 goals in the AHL season. At 28, Leonard is not a true prospect. But the consistency of his scoring — 87 goals in his last 132 AHL games — makes you wonder whether the Red Wings will consider bringing him and playing him with other skilled players. He’s had other call-ups but not really played enough minutes to show what he can do. With the Red Wings struggling offensively, this might be the season to give him an extended shot. John Leonard now boasts 24 game-winning goals over those 132 AHL games. He has a knack of scoring big goals. He leads the league in game-winners (eight) this season Defenseman Axel Sandin-Pellikka and center Nate Danielson registered two assists each to help the Griffins win their seventh consecutive game. Grand Rapids is 17-2-1-1 on the season. Danielson had eight points (2-6–8) in his past four games. Michal Postava made 26 saves to improve his record to 9-0. Carter Bear also scored his sixth goal of the season. item.title: Jiri Lehecka leads Czechs to Davis Cup quarter-final victory over 2022 winners Canada
item.description: Czech No 1 Jiri Lehecka beat Felix Auger-Aliassime 7-6(4) 6-2 to seal a 2-0 quarter-final victory for Czechia over Canada in the Davis Cup . The world No 14’s victory ensured Czechia booked their place in the last four of tennis’ ‘World Cup’ for the first time in more than a decade. Earlier on Tuesday Tomas Mahac beat Liam Draxl 6-2 3-6 6-2 to put the Czechs in front, with Lehecka’s straightforward win meaning there was no need for the dead-rubber doubles match to be played, with Davis Cup ties best of three. Czechia will now play either three-time defending champions Italy, led by Flavio Cobolli, or South Korea, who face off on Wednesday. The semi-final will take place on Friday. Auger-Aliassime, a former world No 4 now ranked 17th, squandered ​nine ⁠break points, including a set ‌point at 5-4 in the opening set, before Lehecka forced a tiebreak. He continued to keep the Canadian under pressure with his aggressive play and powerful forehand, earning an early break before going 3-0 up in the second set, and converted his second match point before celebrating with his teammates. Lehecka said: “It was a super tough match. I was forced to play very well facing some break points and some tough situations. “Felix is such a dangerous player in these conditions, so I’m very proud with the way I converted the chances I had in the first set and also how I was able to improve my game in the second. I think it’s a great win, not just for me but for the whole team and I’m very, very proud of the team.” Earlier Machac, the mixed doubles champion from the 2024 Paris Olympics, made a flying start against world No 154 Draxl, surging into a 4-0 lead in ‌the first set. But what had looked like an easy win for the Czech turned into a real battle as Draxl fought back to force a decider. Machac regained control by breaking ‌for a 4-2 lead ​in the third before sealing ‌victory in an hour and 55 minutes.
